action_items.item: Find out why the spend-totals cache stopped applying purchases from the ledger at about the onset time, using the cache's own update path and the writer that feeds it. Confirm whether the proposed fix addresses that mechanism.
Run the cache-versus-ledger reconciliation check continuously, and keep a repair path that corrects stale entries automatically, instead of relying on discarding entries by hand after an alert.

Add a freshness signal for the cache, such as lag between the latest ledger purchase and the latest purchase the cache has applied, and alert on it so a stall pages within minutes rather than after the reconciliation check.

Make sure metrics, logs and cache update events for this service are retained and readable by Argus, and record in the investigation when a channel returns nothing so an empty read is not taken as a clean one.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers were shown cached spend totals that were behind their real purchases. {A1} of {A2} checked figures disagreed with the ledger, each missing at most {A4} purchase, with a widest gap of {A3}. No request failed, so only the alert's reconciliation check showed it.

The cached copies were wrong because the cache was no longer being updated from the purchase ledger. The oldest purchase the copies did not account for was recorded at {A5}, and the ledger stayed correct throughout. Any shopper who bought again after that point had a stale figure.

The record cannot say why the cache stopped keeping up. It shows no production change, no log lines and no readable metrics for the window, and the second candidate (no observable cause) was never tried. The chain stops here.

contributing_factors.factor: Nothing reconciles or repairs the cached copies once they fall behind. The alert states that a figure goes stale as soon as its shopper buys again, so the discard was only a stopgap and the fault can recur. The open fix is the only record item aimed at this, and its effect is unverified.

Detection was late. The copies stopped keeping up at about {A5} and were served from {A6}, but the alert only fired at {alert_raised}, after stale figures were already being shown. No service metric moves when the cache goes stale, so only the reconciliation check can notice.

Telemetry for the investigation was missing. Per-minute metrics, logs and change events all came back empty, so the Investigator could not explain the stall and could only describe it as a state divergence.

input.executive_summary: Some shoppers were shown out-of-date spend totals. At the alert, {A1} of {A2} cached figures disagreed with the purchases behind them. Each was missing at most {A4} purchase, and the widest gap was {A3}. The purchases themselves were always correct. The copies stopped updating at about {A5} and were being served from {A6}. The alert fired at {alert_raised}, and the impact lasted at least {duration}, which is a lower bound. Argus discarded the stale copies so those pages read from the purchase ledger again, and the store confirmed it removed them. Argus's handling took {held}. The reason the cache stopped updating was not found. A draft fix has been proposed and is awaiting review, and nothing yet keeps the copies correct if they go stale again.

got_lucky: The ledger was never affected, so discarding the copies was a safe way to restore correct figures. A fault in the ledger itself would have had no such easy way out.
Each stale figure was missing at most {A4} purchase, so the errors were small.
went_well: Argus picked up the alert within seconds and discarded the stale copies, so affected pages went back to the ledger, which was always correct.
The mitigation was confirmed by the store reporting what it removed, and a draft fix was proposed straight away.
went_wrong: The cause of the stall was never identified. The metrics, logs and change reads all came back empty, and the leading candidate rests on the alert's own data.
The discard does not stop new staleness, so a later check may name more entries until the cause is fixed.
The stall went unnoticed from the time the copies stopped keeping up until the alert fired.

input.root_cause: The cache of shopper spend totals stopped keeping up with the purchase ledger at about {A5} and kept serving stale figures from then on. The record holds no deploy, flag change, log line or metric that shows why it stopped, so the mechanism behind the stall is not established.
